channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: House Republicans Seek More Changes at Hobbled Consumer Watchdog
item.description: A group of House Republicans unveiled a proposal that aims to overhaul the structure of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which has been entangled in legal fights as the Trump administration moves to cut the agency’s funding and staffing.
item.dc:creator: J.J. McCorvey

item.title: European Gas Futures Rise to Highest Since 2023 on Iran War
item.description: European natural gas benchmark futures surged to their highest since January 2023 as the US launched a fresh wave of strikes against Iran.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Liao and Priscila Azevedo Rocha

item.title: Bitcoin ETF Buyers Return as $80,000 Level Tests Market Rally
item.description: The investors who helped propel Bitcoin into its Wall Street era are showing signs of coming back, offering a crucial test of whether its latest rally can turn into something bigger.
item.dc:creator: Isabelle Lee and Philip Lagerkranser

item.title: SEC Preps Plan to Widen Investor Access to Private Markets
item.description: The US Securities and Exchange Commission is eyeing a plan to expand access for retail investors to private markets and allow investment advisers to charge performance fees to a wider set of clients.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: Trump Iran Messaging 'Extremely Reckless,' Says Rep. Madeleine Dean
item.description: Pennsylvania Democrat Madeleine Dean, who sits on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said the US and its Middle Eastern allies 'are all less safe as a result of this war in Iran' and called the president's messaging around the war 'extremely reckless.' The congresswoman also weighed in on the potential for increased sanctions against Russia, saying that she does not think that the bill will come to a vote this week and that she is wary of the increased tariff authority it would give President Trump, despite her calls for support for Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Government Bond Yields Are Rising and Causing Alarm
item.description: Government borrowing costs have been surging around the world as investors demand more compensation to entice them to hold longer-maturity debt. Yields on 30-year Japanese government bonds are near all-time highs at 4.19%, while 30-year UK government bond yields are at their highest since 1998. A Bloomberg gauge tracking government debt across the Group of Seven countries now yields its highest on average since September 2000.
item.dc:creator: George Nixon, Ye Xie and Greg Ritchie

item.title: US Strikes Targets in Iran Around Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The US launched strikes against Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz, following Iran's attacks on commercial shipping and American forces in the region. Oil prices are spiking on the news. Tyler Kendall reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Global Bond Rout Sends Yields Soaring | Open Interest 9/1/2026
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Global bonds tumble as yields surge to levels not seen since 2008, with soaring oil and renewed Middle East tensions fueling the selloff. Plus, a new era at Apple as John Ternus takes the reins. We’ll dig into Bobby Jain’s Millennium deal and the private-markets shakeout with Achilles Global Management CIO Sachin Khajuria. Plus, David Layton, the CEO of the Partners Group joins us to push back on concerns his move to CIO signals trouble. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fortress’s Burton Says Rates Still Poised to Go Higher
item.description: Global bonds slumped as rising oil prices fueled inflation fears and bets on Fed rate hikes. Fortress Chief Strategist Elizabeth Burton says rates are still poised to go higher, arguing the underlying problem won’t be fixed without a fiscal response. She speaks on Bloomberg Open Interest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bond Market Selloff: Are Surging Yields a Threat to the Global Stock Rally?
item.description: In equity markets, the myth goes that the only way is up. That perception has gained traction as global stock prices have largely ignored the selloff in bond markets. Yields on long-dated government debt have surged to near two-decade highs as investors worry about whether inflation and fiscal deficits can be tamed, and as sovereign bonds compete with an AI-fueled corporate borrowing boom.
item.dc:creator: Sagarika Jaisinghani, Alice Gledhill and Margaryta Kirakosian

item.title: Oil Prices Spike as US Retaliates for Attacks by Iran
item.description: Oil rose for a second session as fresh hostilities between the US and Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, where crude carriers were hit by projectiles. Leslie Palti-Guzman, Founder at Energy Vista, discusses the outlook for global energy as conflict in the Middle East continues to disrupt flow. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wells Fargo Analysts Join JPMorgan Traders in Turning Cautious on US Stocks
item.description: Wells Fargo & Co. joins a growing chorus of voices that are cautioning on US stocks this week as the market heads into what is historically the worst month on the calendar for equities and upcoming midterm elections add to uncertainty surrounding the artificial-intelligence trade.
item.dc:creator: Emily Forgash

item.title: Senegal to Rework Debt as It Reaches New IMF Deal
item.description: Senegal’s eurobonds fell on Tuesday after the government said it will move forward with a “debt treatment” under the Group of 20’s Common Framework and agreed a new $2.2 billion program with the International Monetary Fund.
item.dc:creator: Katarina Höije, Jorgelina do Rosario and Ray Ndlovu

item.title: Peru Inflation Just Tops Estimate to Hit Fastest Since 2023
item.description: Inflation in Peru’s capital accelerated slightly more than expected in August, hitting the fastest pace in almost three years, pressured by housing and utilities including electricity and gas.
item.dc:creator: Carla Samon Ros

item.title: Dell, HP Enterprise Need Earnings to Validate Record Stock Runs
item.description: Artificial intelligence fever is powering Dell Technologies Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. to their best years in the stock market.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: Nasdaq 100 Drops as Traders Assess Oil Spike, Bond Jitters
item.description: The Nasdaq 100 Index is retreating on Tuesday after coming off session lows, as investors weigh the effects of rising bond yields and higher oil prices on the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Menton

item.title: Bond Slide Spreads to Emerging Markets on Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: A global bond selloff spread to emerging markets as investors dumped the riskier debt on expectations that the Federal Reserve will increase US interest rates later this month.
item.dc:creator: Srinivasan Sivabalan and Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo

item.title: Gold Approaches Two-Week Low on Rising Yields, Fed Hike Bets
item.description: Gold fell to the lowest in almost two weeks as a global bond selloff sent yields higher, with traders betting the Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates to contain inflationary pressure from elevated oil prices.
item.dc:creator: Yvonne Yue Li

item.title: Stocks, Bonds Fall as Oil Jumps on US-Iran Jitters: Markets Wrap
item.description: A surge in oil prices rippled through global markets, hitting stocks and bonds on worries that higher energy costs will fuel inflation and force the Federal Reserve to boost rates.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 1
item.description: US oil prices topped $90 a barrel for the first time since late July as fresh American strikes on Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Mia Gindis, Charles Gorrivan and Paul Burkhardt
